channel.title: The Kimberley Echo - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Kimberley Echo (kimberleyecho.com.au)

item.title: Supporting healing and connection in Fitzroy Crossing
item.description: This year the Kimberley Aboriginal Medical Services Social (KAMS) and Emotional Wellbeing (SEWB) Team has continued to make an impact across Fitzroy Crossing and surrounding communities

item.title: Mount Anderson helicopter crash: Cause of collision that killed pilots Peter Ritter, Gavin U’Ren revealed
item.description: Pilots Peter Ritter and Gavin U’Ren died after their helicopters collided mid-air last year.

item.title: East Kimberley men’s forum builds connection, healing, and cultural pride
item.description: Men across the East Kimberley recently came together for the second annual Stronger in Our Way Men’s Forum, a two-day event focused on connection, healing and strengthening cultural identity.

item.title: Celebrating cultural education
item.description: A dedicated team of seven educators from Purnululu School travelled to Auckland, New Zealand, to take part in the highly anticipated World Indigenous Peoples’ Conference on Education

item.title: Community sitting firmly at the centre of discussions about Kununurra night space
item.description: Community voices are sitting firmly at the centre of discussions about how Kununurra’s new night space facility — including how should look, where it should be located and how it should operate

item.title: Halls Creek Oval upgrades receive extra funding to complete works before 2026 football season
item.description: Halls Creek Oval will be upgraded and ready to go for the 2026 football season with the State Government kicking in more than $400,000 in additional funding to get the work done.

item.title: Renaming on the cards for locations linked to brothers accused of violent Kimberley killings
item.description: Road names linked to a bloody period of Kimberley history could finally be set to change.

item.title: Mayi Kuwayu Study roadshow engages Kimberley and Pilbara communities
item.description: Thew Mayi Kuwayu Study, Australia’s largest national research project on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander culture, health and wellbeing, is making its way through the Kimberley and Pilbara

item.title: Cloud hangs over Derby council election result as WAEC ‘invalidity complaint’ revealed
item.description: The October elections were supposed to herald a fresh start for the beleaguered Shire of Derby, but less than a month after electors headed to the polls the WAEC has filed an “invalidity complaint”.

item.title: Kimberley Remote Aboriginal Communities Leaders Network launches in Broome
item.description: A new community-led initiative, the Kimberley Remote Aboriginal Communities Leaders Network, was launched at Nirrumbuk Environmental Health and Services in Broome on December 3.
